regulatoryRegime.repealedRegulation: NEPRA (Alternative & Renewable Energy) Distributed Generation and Net Metering Regulations, 2015 (S.R.O. 812(I)/2015)

billingMechanism.description: Imports and exports are billed separately. Grid imports are billed at applicable consumer retail slab tariffs; surplus exports are credited separately at buyback rate. Net monetary balance is billed/credited.
billingMechanism.grossMeteringStatus: Not implemented. Mid-2024 Power Division gross metering proposals were shelved in favor of net billing (self-consumption behind the meter is retained).

exportRate.determinationMethod: National Average Energy Purchase Price (NAEPP / EPP) / avoided variable fuel generation cost, excluding capacity charges and T&D margins

source.title: NEPRA (Prosumer) Regulations, 2026 & Power Purchase Price Benchmarks

settlementPeriod.creditRollover: Surplus monetary export credit carries forward to offset subsequent monthly electricity bills

turnkeyLiaisonFeePkr.note: Private EPC liaison & documentation fee (secondary source / market estimate)

source.title: DISCO Guidelines (LESCO/IESCO/FESCO) & NEPRA Schedule of Fees

grandfathering.eligibleUsers: Distributed generation consumers with valid net metering agreements executed under the 2015 regulations prior to February 9, 2026
grandfathering.protectedTerms: Retain 1:1 volumetric unit-for-unit net metering mechanism
grandfathering.expiry: Valid until the expiration of the original agreement tenure (standard 7 years from agreement date)
grandfathering.forfeitureCondition: Any material modification or increase to maximum generation output/capacity revokes grandfathering and migrates facility to 2026 net billing

source.title: NEPRA S.R.O. 547(I)/2026 (Amendment to Prosumer Regulations, Regulation 21)
